# Additions to Daniel Chapter 2 (Susanna) — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus (Theodotion recension), Additions to Daniel 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADD_002_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition 2: Susanna. A self-contained novella about justice, female courage, and Daniel's wisdom as a young judge.]*

**1** There was a man living in Babylon whose name was Joiakim.

**2** He had taken as his wife a woman named Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah — beautiful in appearance and God-fearing.

**3** Her parents were righteous and had raised their daughter according to the law of Moses.

**4** Joiakim was very wealthy and had a garden adjacent to his house; the Jews used to gather there because he was the most respected of them all.

**5** In that year two of the elders were appointed from among the people to serve as judges — the very sort about whom the Lord had spoken: "Lawlessness came out from Babylon, from elders who were judges, who only seemed to govern the people."

**6** These men frequented the house of Joiakim, and all who had legal disputes came to them.

**7** At midday, when the people withdrew, Susanna would go in and walk in her husband's garden.

**8** The two elders saw her every day going in and walking about, and they became consumed with desire for her.

**9** They corrupted their own minds and averted their eyes from heaven, refusing to remember their duty to render just judgments.

**10** Both of them were tortured with passion for her, yet neither disclosed his grief to the other,

**11** for each was ashamed to confess his desire — his longing to lie with her.

**12** Day after day they watched for an opportunity to see her.

**13** One day they said to each other, "Let us go home, for it is the dinner hour." And departing, they each went his own way —

**14** only to double back and meet at the same place. Pressing each other for reasons, they each admitted their desire; and from then on they watched together, setting a time when they would find her alone.

**15** One day, when they were watching for the right opportunity, she came in as she usually did, with only two maidservants, and wished to bathe in the garden, for the day was hot.

**16** No one else was there but the two elders, who had concealed themselves and were watching her.

**17** She said to her maidservants: "Bring me oil and ointments, and close the garden doors so that I may bathe."

**18** They did as she instructed: they shut the garden doors and went out by the side entrances to fetch what she had asked for; they did not see the elders, because they were hidden.

**19** As soon as the maidservants had gone, the two elders sprang up and rushed to her, saying:

**20** "Look — the garden doors are shut, and no one can see us; we desire you, so consent to us and lie with us.

**21** If you refuse, we will testify against you that a young man was here with you, and that is why you sent the maidservants away."

**22** Susanna groaned and said: "I am hemmed in on every side. If I do this, it means death for me; and if I refuse, I will not escape your hands.

**23** Yet it is better for me to fall into your hands without doing it than to sin in the sight of the Lord."

**24** Then Susanna screamed at the top of her voice; and the two elders shouted back against her.

**25** One of them ran and threw open the garden doors.

**26** When the household servants heard the commotion in the garden, they rushed in through the side entrances to see what had happened to her.

**27** When the elders told their story, the servants were mortified, because nothing of this kind had ever been said about Susanna.

**28** The next day, when the people assembled at the house of her husband Joiakim, the two elders arrived filled with their wicked scheme to have Susanna put to death.

**29** They said before the people: "Send for Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, the wife of Joiakim." And they sent for her.

**30** She came with her father and mother, her children, and all her relatives.

**31** Now Susanna was very graceful and beautiful.

**32** The wicked men ordered her to be unveiled — for she was veiled — so that they might feast their eyes on her beauty.

**33** Those with her and all who knew her were weeping.

**34** The two elders stood up before the assembly and laid their hands on her head.

**35** She wept and looked up toward heaven, for her heart trusted in the Lord.

**36** The elders said: "We were walking alone in the garden when this woman came in with two maidservants. She shut the garden doors and dismissed the maidservants.

**37** Then a young man who had been in hiding came to her and lay with her.

**38** We were in a corner of the garden, and when we saw this wicked deed we ran toward them.

**39** We saw them coupling together, but the man we could not hold, for he was stronger than us; he threw open the doors and fled.

**40** But we seized this woman and demanded to know who the young man was.

**41** She refused to tell us. This is our testimony."

**42** The assembly believed them, since they were elders of the people and judges; and they sentenced her to death.

**43** Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice and said: "O eternal God, who know what is hidden, who know all things before they come to pass —

**44** you know that these men have given false testimony against me. And now I am to die, though I have done none of the things they have wickedly charged against me."

**45** And the Lord heard her voice.

**46** As she was being led away to death, God stirred up the holy spirit of a young man named Daniel,

**47** and he called out with a loud voice: "I am innocent of this woman's blood!"

**48** All the people turned to him and asked: "What are you saying?"

**49** Standing in their midst, he said: "Are you such fools, O sons of Israel? Have you condemned a daughter of Israel without proper examination, without even establishing the truth?

**50** Go back to the court — these men have given false testimony against her."

**51** The people all turned back in haste. And the elders said to Daniel: "Come, sit with us and tell us what you have found, since God has given you the standing of an elder."

**52** Daniel said to them: "Separate them from each other. I will examine them."

**53** Once they had been separated, he called the first elder and said to him: "You who have grown old in wickedness, now at last your sins of former years have caught up with you —

**54** rendering unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and acquitting the guilty — when the Lord said, 'The innocent and the righteous you shall not put to death.'

**55** Now then — if you truly saw this woman, tell me: under what tree did you see them together?" He answered, "Under a mastic tree [schinos]." Daniel said: "Your lie has condemned you, for the angel of God has received the sentence from God and will split you in two [schizein]."

**56** He set that one aside and called the other, and said to him: "You offspring of Canaan and not of Judah — beauty has seduced you and lust has corrupted your heart.

**57** This is how you treated the daughters of Israel, and they lay with you out of fear; but a daughter of Judah would not endure your lawlessness.

**58** Now tell me: under what tree did you catch them together?" He answered, "Under a holm oak [prinos]." Daniel said: "Your lie has condemned you too, for the angel of God waits with his sword to cut you in two [priein], and destroy you both."

**59** All the assembly cried out with a great voice and blessed God, who saves those who hope in him.

**60** They rose up against the two elders, for out of their own mouths Daniel had convicted them of giving false testimony.

**61** They did to them as they had wickedly plotted to do to their neighbor, acting in accordance with the law of Moses; and they put them to death. Thus innocent blood was spared that day.

**62** Hilkiah and his wife gave praise to God for their daughter Susanna, together with her husband Joiakim and all her relatives, because no disgraceful thing had been found in her.

**63** From that day on Daniel was held in great esteem by the people.

**64** And King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received the kingdom.
